analysis.title: Caution Warranted Absent Sponsorship; Systematic Selling Largely Behind
key_insights: None of the circuit breakers UBS flagged two months ago as catalysts to fresh highs have manifested. Rate pressure turned into funding pressure, oil rose as the Mideast conflict continued, hyperscaler earnings fell short, and Democrats dominated the mid-terms.
Investors are demanding a large discount to add AI risk despite continued AI demand. Incremental dollars have moved away from Tech and from equities into credit, where AI exposure is growing quickly.

Systematic selling on Thursday produced over $365bn of SPX excess sell flow, the largest on record. UBS says most systematic selling is behind the market, with a residual amount on Monday, given current exposures in risk control funds and CTAs.

The bigger issue is the absence of long-only demand, which UBS calls the focal point for flows from here. It is unclear how much of a rebound is possible from rotations and fading systematic selling alone.
UBS expects US equities to stay vulnerable in early trading this week, with another test of technical support and the 200-day moving average likely. Squeeze risk is described as acute.
If the clearing event comes without deterioration in credit, rates or FX, UBS says to add risk rather than protection.
The market rotated into quality during the AI de-risking, both within AI and across sectors. Hyperscalers outperformed the broader AI complex, especially funding-dependent neoclouds.

After the hyperscaler outperformance and semiconductors giving back most of the post-April rally, rotation from hyperscalers back into semis has started. Friday's 5% semis outperformance versus a flat hyperscaler basket is called an important rotational turning point.
Rebecca Cheong's VIX cross-asset score hit 96% on Thursday. UBS says that level typically signals capitulatory price action, with 1M forward returns favoring lower VIX at a +90% hit rate.
2026 is tied with 2017 for the fewest days on which all sectors fell in one session, which UBS cites as a reason SPX was overdue for a correlated selloff.
The correlated drop was hard on short-vol strategies. Dispersion strategies were mixed because single-stock long-vol selection drove the differences in returns.

UBS's Bespoke Dispersion Strategy index (XUBSDVS4), which isolates popular structured-product names (largely Tech/AI), hit an all-time high Thursday and Friday as single-stock moves far exceeded SPX's -4.4% implied move. UBS calls it a positive-expectation hedge to AI exposure.
CPI and NVDA earnings on the 17th are the next two risk events, with SPX pricing about 1% daily moves for both, among the highest through year-end.
UBS economist Alan expects a softer October CPI at +0.23% core and +0.26% headline, helped by gasoline and used vehicles.
Macro focus has returned to the long end after strong NFP. A 10Y retest of recent highs would be a clear headwind for risk.
Neoclouds and speculative growth names were the big Friday outperformers at +10% and +11%, but the note says nothing has really changed.
UBS's long/short quality factor is starting to fade, and the note says defensive sectors such as healthcare and staples are vulnerable while semis are poised to rebound.

sector_views.rationale: Semis gave back most of the post-April rally and outperformed hyperscalers by 5% on Friday. UBS says they are poised to rebound and outperform hyperscalers.
Outperformance versus the broad AI complex is described as likely overextended, with a possible catch-down.
Safety sectors are overbought after quality outperformed, and UBS calls them vulnerable.

earnings_insights: Hyperscaler earnings fell short over the past two months, per UBS. No figures are given.
NVDA earnings are on 11/17 (forecast event). SPX is pricing about a 1% one-day move around the print and CPI, among the highest through year-end.

macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS economist Alan expects a softer print, helped by gasoline and used vehicles.
A softer print would ease pressure on the long end, which is the macro focus after strong NFP.
The strong print returned focus to the long end of the Treasury curve.
A retest would be a clear headwind for risk.

risk_factors: Absence of long-only demand limits any rebound.
A 10Y yield retest of recent highs after strong NFP.
Hot October CPI or a weak NVDA print on the 17th, with about 1% daily moves priced for each.
Rate pressure turning into funding pressure, and rising AI exposure in credit.
Continued Mideast conflict and elevated oil prices.
Failure of the 200-day moving average, with a deterioration in credit, rates or FX.
vol_and_positioning: SPX excess sell flow from systematic selling hit -$365bn on Thursday, a record, with virtually no reversal Friday. NDX excess sell flow was -$203bn.
Risk control funds and CTAs are largely done selling at current exposures, with a residual amount expected Monday.
VIX cross-asset score (Rebecca Cheong) hit 96% Thursday. 1M forward returns favor lower VIX with a +90% hit rate at that level.
SPX is pricing about 1% daily moves for CPI and NVDA earnings on the 17th, among the highest through year-end.
Squeeze risk is acute around the expected 200-day moving average test.
XUBSDVS4 dispersion index hit all-time highs Thursday and Friday. It remains a positive-expectation hedge to AI exposures.
geopolitical: Mideast conflict continued and oil prices soared over the past two months.

tension_points.bull_case: Systematic selling is largely behind the market, the VIX cross-asset score at 96% points to capitulation with a +90% hit rate for lower VIX, and squeeze risk is acute. UBS says to add risk if the 200-day test clears without credit, rates or FX deterioration.
tension_points.bear_case: Long-only demand is absent and it is unclear how much rebound is possible from rotation and fading systematic selling alone. A 10Y retest of recent highs, CPI and NVDA earnings are further risks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deterioration in credit, rates or FX alongside the 200-day moving average test, or a 10Y retest of recent highs.

tension_points.bull_case: Semis gave up most of the post-April rally and outperformed hyperscalers by 5% on Friday, which UBS calls an important rotational turning point.
tension_points.bear_case: Rotation could instead become a hyperscaler catch-down versus a broad-based rally if inflows do not come.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Long-only inflows failing to emerge for a broad-based rally.
